text:
maria: Hey team — seeing repeated 403s when our prod worker (AKS, user-assigned MI) calls Azure Key Vault over a Private Endpoint to unwrap envelope keys. Works from dev cluster but fails in prod. anyone seen privatelink + msi weirdness?
kevin: Can you paste the exact error from the token/kv logs?
maria: Logs: `2024-08-12T14:21:03Z ERROR KeyVault: UnwrapKey failed - AuthorizationPermissionMismatch (403) - Principal not authorized to perform operation`. No other details in app logs.
shan: Probably a permission model mismatch — is the vault using Access Policies or Azure RBAC?
maria: Not sure, how do I check quickly?
kevin: az cli: `az keyvault show -n my-kv -g prod-rg --query properties.enableRbacAuthorization` (if true => RBAC; if false => access policies). Also `az keyvault show -n my-kv --query properties` to see firewall/private endpoint settings.
maria: Confirmed: enableRbacAuthorization = true.
kevin: Ok then access policies are ignored. You need to assign an RBAC role that grants crypto permissions (wrap/unwrap/get). The built-in role is `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` or sometimes `Key Vault Crypto User` depending on SKU — check portal for 'Keys' roles.
shan: Example role assignment: `az role assignment create --assignee <msi_principalId> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/my-kv`
maria: We already gave the MI Reader on the RG but not that crypto role. Could that explain why dev works?
kevin: Possibly. Dev might have access via an access policy (old vault) or you granted the role at subscription level there. RBAC is scoped; role must include key operations.
elena: Also check the key version — envelope metadata might reference a specific key version that no longer exists or was rotated. If the request uses a key id that doesn't match current version you can get key-not-found or permission errors too.
maria: The app sends full key id from DB: https://my-kv.vault.azure.net/keys/envelopeKey/1234567890abcdef. That looks current.
shan: Another angle: Private Endpoint + DNS. When AKS uses privatelink, traffic goes private; Key Vault will still validate the AAD token. If the managed identity is from a different tenant (guest principal) the principal might not be in the Key Vault tenant's AAD — result: authorization denied. Are your prod AKS and KV in different tenants or subscriptions?
maria: Both in same tenant/sub, same subscription.
kevin: Then check the service principal/objectId you assigned the role to: is it the user-assigned MI's principalId (object id) or the clientId? Role assignment needs the principalId or principal name. `az identity show -g rg -n uami --query principalId` to confirm.
maria: I used the clientId. Oof. Trying with principalId now.
infra-bot: deploy:role-assignment job queued for uami-principalId on my-kv (job id 0a1b2c) :gear:
kevin: Also check activity logs in the Key Vault diagnostic logs (AzureDiagnostics table) — look for AuthorizationDecision entries. It often includes missing action: e.g., denied for action `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action` or `unwrap`.
shan: If you still get denied after role assignment, confirm the role includes these actions. If not, create a custom role with allowedActions: `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action`, `.../unwrap/action`, `.../get` and assign at vault scope.
elena: For cross-tenant scenarios the recommended pattern is workload identity federation (if using pods) or create a service principal in the target tenant. Guest MIs sometimes lack AAD object in the tenant vault expects.
maria: Role assignment finished. Re-ran job, still 403 but logs show slightly different: `Denied - Key operation: unwrap, reason: PrincipalIdMismatch`
kevin: PrincipalIdMismatch suggests the token's oid (object id) doesn't match the principal you assigned the role to. Are you minting tokens for the system-assigned MI instead of the user-assigned? Or is the pod using aad-pod-identity and mapping to wrong identity?
maria: We're using aad-pod-identity with binding label app=encryptor. I think one of the pods got bound to system-assigned MI in prod.
shan: Quick check: inside pod `curl "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fvault.azure.net" -H Metadata:true` and inspect `oid` in token. Compare with `az identity show` principalId.
maria: Doing that now... token oid != principalId. That was it. We had a race during deploy where the user-assigned identity wasn't attached to the node pool before pod started.
kevin: Fix: ensure node pool has AAD MI pre-attached or use projected token provider (AAD Workload Identity) to avoid node-level attachment race. Also add a startup check in the app to verify token oid matches expected principalId.
maria: After reattaching identity and restarting pod, unwrap succeeded. Thanks all! :tada:
elena: For postmortem, let's add these items to runbook: (1) verify KV permission model (RBAC vs access policy) (2) required role(s) for un/wrap (3) validate MI principalId/token oid at startup (4) DNS/privatelink checklist (5) key version verification in envelope metadata.
maria: I'll open a short runbook PR and add an alert to watch for repeated 403 unwraps.
kevin: One more: enable KeyVault diagnostic logs routed to Log Analytics and set a query alert on `Category == 'AuditEvent' and OperationName contains 'UnwrapKey' and ResultType == '403'` so infra can page.
maria: Will do. Marking this thread resolved for now. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
